points.description: States the core fact: a queue is a data structure (collection of elements) that follows the first in, first out (FIFO) principle, i.e. the first element added is the first removed. Any wording that conveys first-in-first-out order counts (e.g. 'first come first served', 'oldest item leaves first').
points.partial_credit: Half marks for a related statement that gets part of the idea, such as 'a line where items are served in order' or 'a structure that stores elements' with no order principle.

rubric.notes: Full marks for stating that a queue stores elements in first-in, first-out order, in any wording, even briefly. Give half marks for a related but incomplete statement, such as describing it only as a collection or line without the order principle. Give no marks if the answer describes a different structure such as a stack (last in, first out) or talks only about operations without the ordering idea. Naming enqueue and dequeue is not required for full marks, and extra correct detail costs nothing.
